scope: Primary-source check of the operator-convex family f_kappa and its possible transfer to physical KMS entropy production versus root Dirichlet energy.

opportunities.claim: For real kappa, f_kappa(t)=(t-1)log(t)-kappa(sqrt(t)-1)^2 is operator convex on (0,infinity) iff kappa<=pi. For faithful finite-dimensional states, this gives quantum Jeffreys divergence >= pi times squared Hilbert-Schmidt distance between square roots.
opportunities.source: Franz-Hiai, arXiv:1310.1539v1, Theorem 2.2, pp. 159-160; Hiai-Mosonyi-Petz-Beny, arXiv:1008.2529v6, Section 2.1 for the Petz f-divergence functional calculus.
opportunities.new_calculation: Specialize the unique representation at alpha=1 with dmu=[1+lambda-(2kappa/pi)sqrt(lambda)]dlambda. Verify the two scalar resolvent integrals; measure positivity gives kappa<=pi and Stieltjes-transform uniqueness excludes kappa>pi.
opportunities.scope_limit: Static state-pair inequality only; no KMS generator appears. The Petz monotonicity theorem in arXiv:1008.2529v6 states a function domain continuous on [0,infinity), whereas this f_kappa diverges at zero; use the direct faithful-pair calculus, not an unproved boundary extension.

opportunities.claim: The static Petz quasi-entropy and its Hessian do not by themselves imply the physical nonlinear estimate J(rho)>=pi E_KMS(rho). Differentiating the static potential leaves a Dlog_rho[L_*(rho)] term and a Dsqrt_rho[L_*(rho)] term; no checked primary result identifies these with the KMS square-root Dirichlet energy for arbitrary KMS generators.
opportunities.load_bearing_interface: A valid transfer must match the physical tangent Z=dot(rho) to the KMS-root variable through Z=sY+Ys (s=sqrt(sigma)), i.e. Y=Lyapunov_s^{-1}(Z), and then control the generator insertion. If a cited source uses Z=sXs, its tangent variable is not Y: Y_ij=s_i s_j/(s_i+s_j)X_ij.
opportunities.source_search_status: Bounded check of Franz-Hiai operator-convex representation and Hiai-Mosonyi-Petz-Beny Petz quasi-entropy/data-processing definitions only; this is not a comprehensive priority audit.
